commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, response formatting, and all user-facing messages out of Serina so the main class can focus on application flow. Keep command behavior and output unchanged, and centralize numbered task rendering to reduce presentation duplication.

Introduce a TaskList abstraction that owns capacity checks, one-based task lookup, deletion, date matching, and collection size. Update Serina to delegate these operations and expose only a read-only task view to the UI and storage, preparing a stable execution API for future Command classes.

Refactor command processing so the GUI and CLI share the same behavior,

Add varargs constructors for command responses and task lists to make
individual-value call sites more concise. Add a varargs test helper to
simplify response assertions while retaining the collection-based APIs.

Add Java assertions around command parsing, task construction,
task-list mutation, storage parsing, and date parsing to make
internal invariants explicit.

Update AI.md to record the assertion work and its rationale.

Review command parsing against the CS2103 code quality guidelines and address the highest-priority readability issue found.

Serina.java repeated command words and argument separators directly inside matching and substring logic. That mixed command intent with low-level string slicing, made the parser harder to scan, and created a maintenance risk if a command word changed in one place but not another.

Introduce named constants for command words and separators, then centralize command matching and argument extraction in helper methods. This keeps the behavior unchanged while reducing duplication and keeping the command dispatch code at a clearer level of abstraction.

Update AI.md to document the refactoring and rationale for future project history.

Review the task hierarchy against the CS2103 code quality guidelines and address duplicated constructor initialization as a standalone refactoring.

The no-status constructors in Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event repeated setup that already existed in the constructors accepting an explicit TaskStatus. That duplication made the classes slightly harder to maintain because invariant checks and default status behavior had more than one place to drift.

Delegate each convenience constructor to the fuller constructor with TaskStatus.NOT_DONE. This keeps the public API and behavior unchanged while giving each class one main initialization path for shared validation and field assignment.

Update AI.md so the refactoring rationale is recorded with the rest of the project history.

Review Storage.java against the CS2103 code quality guidelines and address the remaining magic numbers in save-file parsing as a standalone refactoring.

The loader previously used bare field indexes and expected record sizes when validating and reconstructing saved tasks. Readers had to infer that 0 meant task type, 1 meant status, 3 meant a deadline date, and 5 meant an event record size.

Introduce named constants for save-file field positions, expected record sizes, and delimiter characters. This makes the file format visible in one place and lets each parsing branch read in terms of the domain instead of numeric positions.

Keep the behavior unchanged and update AI.md so the code quality rationale is documented in the project history.

Review Serina.java against the CS2103 code quality guidelines and address the mixed abstraction level in processCommand as a standalone refactoring.

The command dispatcher previously decided which command was entered while also performing task mutation, persistence, and response formatting inline. That made the method longer and asked readers to move between high-level dispatch logic and lower-level command details in the same block.

Move each command action into a helper named for the operation it performs. The dispatcher now reads as a clear sequence of command choices, while each helper keeps the command-specific work localized and small.

Keep command behavior and user-facing responses unchanged, and update AI.md with the rationale for the refactoring.

Review Storage.java against the CS2103 code quality guidelines and address repeated validation logic as a standalone refactoring.

The parseTask switch previously repeated field-count checks, required-field checks, and load-failure handling inside each task-type branch. That made the branches harder to scan because validation mechanics obscured the task reconstruction happy path.

Move the repeated checks into validateFieldCount and validateNonEmptyField. The switch branches now state the required save-file shape first and then construct the matching task, while malformed records still produce the same load error.

Update AI.md so the rationale for this code quality iteration is captured in the project history.

Refactor task search and save-line conversion to use stream pipelines
for collection operations that are naturally expressed as filtering and
mapping.

This keeps behavior unchanged while documenting the A-Streams level in
AI.md. Parsing and UI loops remain explicit because their validation,
checked exceptions, and control flow are easier to read as loops.
